questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There were several aspects:

1. I wanted to go to a place with beautiful nature nearby so that I could hike, ski and explore the city in the free time.

2. I wanted to try the real american campus experience, where you get to live on campus and experience the small city that the campus is.

3. I wanted to go to a place with many exchange students, danish as well as others.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exchange was the best thing, if you are ever considering it, do it! The only reason why I gave it 9/10 instead of 10/10 was the academic level - The subjects was quite easy, but then again, you are on exchange, so what does it matter.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. It was hard to find out which requirements KU had as well as the host university. Often we found out we had to do things upon arrival by talking to former exchange students in Denmark and by hearing from others and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. We received the key for our housing and were told there was an introduction day for exchange students, but other than that we pretty much had to figure out most of it ourselves. But I'll say, the introduction day ("Imagine Day") was quite good, and we were told all the necessary things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance before arrival was not good. I reckon it would be quite easy to make a "to-do" list or a document where you wrote all the things exchange students would have to do before arriving. But upon arrival the assistance was decent.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
There was a lot of different residence. The supply is quite low compared to the demand, so quite a few people didn't get on-campus housing although they applied for it.

I stayed at the residence "Fairview Crescent" - Write it down! It's the best and most cozy residence, almost all of the exchange students live there and the atmosphere and community is so nice. And they have a great coffee shop if you have to study (The beanery)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was a meal plan at Fairview. If you get another housing with an option for meal plan, go investigate if it makes sense to add. Sometimes it might be cheaper than buying food yourself, and it sounds nice to have dinner together every night.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It's most often a lot cheaper than finding housing yourself - So I would highly recommend applying for on- campus housing.

AND again, if you are applying, Fairview Crescent is the place!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration proces was quite easy. The most difficult thing was to have them approved at KU.

As soon as KU approved the courses you add register yourself on the courses on UBC's site and hope there is spots available for them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, there wasn't any help from UBC but it wasn't necessary either.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Of all the courses KU approved there was only 1 course that I wasn't able to get - But I just choose another one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just don't be late for two reasons: First of all, the pre-approval process from KU is pretty long, so it's stressful if you don't have time. Second of all, if you are not in good time most of the courses might be full and you will end up with some random ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was quite easy, so if you want to get challenged do not hesitate to take som courses a little higher than usual.

As a bachelor student on my fifth semester I had 3 300-level courses and 1 400-level course. The 400 level was quite hard, while the other ones was pretty easy. But don't worry, as an exchange student they will probably pass you if you give an effort and just talk to them.

Also, I would recommend taking something that interests you. Although it might sounds nice that it's easy, you will loose interest quickly if it's both easy and not in your interest.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In all the courses you had midterms (1 or 2) and a final. So in all our courses the final only weighted 30% or 40% which is very different compared to UCPH where you only have a final weighting 100%.

Also, on UCPH you often have a mix between lectures and teaching in classes. In all of my courses at UBC there were only lectures. There was also so called "Office-hours" which is a little similar to teaching hours at UCPH but they mostly just focus on your questions instead of doing Problem Sets or discussions.

Normally, in many courses, there is also participation, which constitutes a share of your overall grade in the subject.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 355: Introcution to International Trade

ECON 333: Economic History of Modern Europe from the Paleolithic to the Industrial Revolution

ECON 371: Economics of the Environment

ECON 421: Introduction to Game Theory and Applications

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECON 333 was quite nice. The lecturer, Mauricio Delichmann, is such a good man with a lot of passion and interest in the subject. Plus, it can get approved as Economic History back on UCPH if you are studying economics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Almost nothing. Only thing was, I knew it was expensive being on exchange, but I had no idea it would be that expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was way more expensive than I thought. Just basic grocery shopping was pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although the academic level isn't as good as UCPH the facilities at UBC is so cool! They have everything. Tennis courts, basketball courts, football and soccer courts, baseball courts, gym, new swimming pool, great study halls and study rooms, a nearby beach, athletics stadium and much more.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is so many clubs to join. On the introduction day ("Imagine day") you get to meet all the clubs and join them. There is more than 350 clubs, but I would highly recommend joining the Outdoor Club which gives you access to cheap rental on hiking and ski stuff.

Also, join the surf flub and go on their surf trip to Tofino!!

Besides the club, there is Frat partys. Although you might seem a little older as a BA or MA student from UCPH you should go, at least a couple of times. Just seeing that the frat-culture actually exists outside of the movies is awesome.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
See my comment above!

Also, play sports. It's such an easy way to get to know other people on campus.

And just attend to the events in the beginning of the term such as Homecoming football game and exchange-betting parties.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go hike in the fall/ spring depending on when you visit, and then go ski in the winter. Use the weekends wisely, you will quickly realise how fast the time goes and how few weekends you suddenly have to do all the nice things.

Here is a few recommendations:

- The most important recommendation is a multiple-day trip to North Cascades National Park in Washington, USA (Do the "Cascade Pass and Sahale Arm Trail", best and most beautiful hiking route we did during the four months)

- Panorama Ridge

- Joffre Lakes

- Vancouver Island

- Banff National Park

- Grouse Mountain

- Cypress Ski Resort (Both for hiking when it's warm and skiing when it's winter)

- Whistler Ski Resort (Both for hiking and skiing, although skiing is coolest. Consider buying the student pass if you are going more than 6 or 7 ski days)

- Tofino (Surfing)

Also, all exchange students have reading break in November. Here, we gathered a group and flew to California while others went to Yukon in northern Canada, but you can get creative!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very ease. The Canadians were very polite. But to be fair, exchange students connect with exchange students, and a lot mostly end up with other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Join clubs! It's all about prioritising, and you have enough time to do it.

Also, play sports. It's such an easy way to get to know other people on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do something in the weekends like hiking or seeing stuff! It's what you are going to remember when you get back.

2. To keep just a little motivation throughout the term choose courses that awakes just a little interest in you.

3. Socialize. The term is going to be so much more fun if you have someone to share it with. So seek clubs, sports, other exchange students and make new friends :))

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends, experiencing a real american campus and experiencing Canada and Vancouver in the weekends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely all the things you had to do before arriving at the university. It was hard to figure out and hard to seek help.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
